beats.caption: Three companies. One broken shipment.
beats.text: Three companies. One broken shipment. And normally, a human copy-pasting between three portals for the rest of the afternoon. This is RelayRoom.

beats.caption: Entitlements are checked server-side, not in the browser.
beats.text: We sign in first. Entitlements are checked on the server, not in the browser. The admin account bypasses billing; the free operator sees the Polar paywall instead.

beats.caption: Three real origins. No shared backend.
beats.text: Up here is the trust bar. Atlas, Northstar, and Vector are three separate origins, each with its own website, its own database, and its own tool count. There is no shared backend behind them.

beats.caption: Read tools now. Write tools only after approval.
beats.text: Open the runtime and you can see exactly what each origin has offered up. Read tools for evidence, write tools for change. RelayRoom asks for these three origins and nothing else.

beats.caption: Real partner pages. Manual controls still work.
beats.text: And the partners are right here, running as real pages in real iframes, with their own manual controls still working. RelayRoom never scrapes their screens.

beats.caption: One read tool per partner. Normalized answers only.
beats.text: Now the actual job. One click. RelayRoom calls exactly one read tool on each partner — the buyer's deadline, the supplier's lots, the carrier's routes — and only the normalized answers ever cross a boundary.

beats.caption: The model selects. It cannot invent.
beats.text: The solver computes every feasible combination first, then hands only those candidates to the model to pick one and explain it. It can select. It cannot invent, and it cannot execute. If the model is unreachable, the deterministic winner stands, and the badge tells you which one you actually got.

beats.caption: 480 units protected · 12 hours early · +8% cost
beats.text: Here is the recovery. Three hundred and ten units from the primary lot, a hundred and seventy from backup, moving on a priority relay. Four hundred and eighty units protected, twelve hours early, at eight percent added cost — inside the buyer's ten percent cap.

beats.caption: Stage → validate → commit, with rollback on every step.
beats.text: Underneath it, the ordered transaction. Stage, validate, commit — every step tagged with the origin that owns it, and every step carrying a compensating rollback. Notice the commit tools are not available yet.

beats.caption: One approval unlocks the write tools.
beats.text: One human approval unlocks them. Watch each partner frame pulse as the commits land, in order, inside the company that owns them.

beats.caption: Every call: origin, input, result, timestamp.
beats.text: Then you get a receipt. Every tool call, with its origin, its input, its result, and its timestamp — and you can export the whole thing as JSON.

beats.caption: Carrier fails → supplier step is compensated.
beats.text: Now the part that actually matters. Turn on the carrier failure rehearsal and run it again. The supplier reservation commits, the carrier tender fails, and RelayRoom reverses the completed supplier step on its own. The buyer commit is never even attempted.

beats.caption: Independent websites cooperating without surrendering control.
beats.text: Three independent websites. One coordinated change. Nobody handed over their data, and a human still said yes. That is what WebMCP makes possible.
